relevance.rationale: Lattice-Liouville paper whose appendix (Sect. 6) is a self-contained treatment of the non-compact quantum dilogarithm e_b(z): the two modular-double shift equations, the unitarity relation, the product-ratio formula, the directional asymptotics at infinity, and an operator five-term (pentagon) identity proved for COMPLEX b (real b then by continuity). Every one of those ingredients is already load-bearing in the corpus: prop:faddeev-phib-uniqueness writes the same product as its definition of Phi_b and names exactly the shift equations + inversion + sigma-unitarity + strip growth as its four rigidity inputs, and rem:q-dilogarithm-pentagon-associator asserts the operator pentagon on a Weyl pair. NOT core, and the distinction matters: those citation sites are already sourced (faddeev1994, faddeev_kashaev1994, faddeev1995), and prop:faddeev-phib-uniqueness deliberately derives its own analytic bounds 'without contour integration'. So this document supplies a better-localised and in one case stronger (complex-b pentagon; sector-wise asymptotics rather than a crude bound) source for material the corpus already has sourced and already proves — real citation value, no new mathematics entering the folio. Corpus-grep run over docs/audits/, content/, computations/, docs/coordination/ for modular-double / Phi_b: the material is present and closed, not open.

keyResults.statement: e_b(z) equals a ratio of two q-exponentials with q = e^{i pi b^2} and qbar = e^{-i pi b^{-2}}, defining a meromorphic function on all of C with an explicit zero/pole lattice.
keyResults.useForFolio: Primary source for the modular-double product that prop:faddeev-phib-uniqueness writes verbatim as its Phi_b, and for the meromorphy + isolated-zeros facts that block currently establishes by hand.

keyResults.statement: Four-sector asymptotic behaviour of e_b(z) as |z| -> infinity, with Gaussian, theta-function and constant regimes selected by arg(z) relative to arg(b).
keyResults.useForFolio: The sector-wise growth input behind prop:faddeev-phib-uniqueness's 'strip growth' hypothesis; applicable on that block's branch Im b^2 > 0 (arg b = pi/4), so it can replace the block's elementary product-norm bound with a literature statement.

keyResults.statement: The operator five-term identity e_b(P) e_b(X) = e_b(X) e_b(P+X) e_b(P) on a Heisenberg pair, with a proof valid for complex b (real b by continuity).
keyResults.useForFolio: Sources the operator pentagon that rem:q-dilogarithm-pentagon-associator states, at the complex-b generality the corpus's fibre-vs-observable split needs (fibre-level q need not be real).

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry exists; the paper's Sect. 6 is the appropriate source for three separate Phi_b facts the corpus uses.
prop:faddeev-phib-uniqueness currently cites only faddeev1995 + faddeev1994 while stating the product formula and the strip-growth hypothesis that this paper's eqs. (21)-(22) give explicitly.

rem:q-dilogarithm-pentagon-associator cites faddeev_kashaev1994 for the operator pentagon; this paper carries a proof at complex b, which is the regime the corpus's fibre-level (non-real q) framing requires.
